title: Recording: I’m Losing You, I’m Moving On, Kiss Kiss Kiss by John Lennon and Yoko Ono | 1980
content:
Hit Factory, New York City
Producers: John Lennon, Yoko Ono, Jack Douglas
Engineer: Lee DeCarlo

A recording session for John Lennon and Yoko Ono’s Double Fantasy album took place on 26 August 1980.

Three songs were worked on, all of which were remakes: ‘I’m Losing You’, ‘I’m Moving On’, and ‘Kiss Kiss Kiss’.

‘I’m Losing You’ had been recorded on 12 August and again on 18 August. This third version was the keeper, and Lennon overdubbed his lead vocals once it was completed.

‘Kiss Kiss Kiss’ had first been recorded on 8 August, and ‘I’m Moving On’ on 12 August.

This was the final tracking session for the album. All future sessions were for overdubs, mixing, or editing.

We finished with all the basic tracks and everyone was about to go to Mr Chow’s, this very exclusive Chinese restaurant in the city. I’m a guy that likes to stay in the background. They were taking a group shot and I stayed in the control room. Everyone assembled and John kept motioning for me to come into the studio for this shot and I refused. John finally said, ‘I’m not gonna take this photo unless you’re in it!’ So I ran into the studio and I’m positioned in the front row. I wouldn’t have that photo today if John didn’t insist on me being in it.
Stan Vincent, Jack Douglas’s business partner
Starting Over, Ken Sharp
